purpose: IAMMAdapter implementation routing swaps through the Curve Router NG (0x16C6521Dff6baB339122a0FE25a9116693265353). Stores one pre-computed route per ordered (tokenIn,tokenOut) pair (path / swapParams / pools). Routes are owner-set because Curve route encoding must be verified off-chain against pool coin indices. Enforces a bidirectional-configuration invariant so a swap in either direction reverts until BOTH directions of the pair are configured -- a strategy needing round-trip swaps cannot be wired to a half-configured adapter.
relatedContractsNotedNotAnalyzed: AMMRoutes.json (off-chain route catalog consumed by deploy scripts)

verifiedProperties.noUnboundedLoops: verified-bounded: setRoute loops a FIXED 11 iterations over path[]; no dynamic/user-sized loops
verifiedProperties.reentrancyGuarded: none (no nonReentrant) -- but stateless per-call: pulls exactly amountIn, forceApprove exactly amountIn, router sends output directly to msg.sender; holds no persistent funds, no state mutated by swap
verifiedProperties.bidirectionalInvariant: verified: swap requires routes[tokenIn][tokenOut].configured AND routes[tokenOut][tokenIn].configured
verifiedProperties.routeValidationOnSet: partial: validates path[0]==tokenIn and last-non-zero(path)==tokenOut; does NOT validate swapParams correctness, pool addresses, coin indices, or reverse-route consistency (off-chain trust)

stateVariables.name: router
stateVariables.invariant: set once, non-zero (constructor require); the sole swap venue; TRUSTED per registry

stateVariables.name: routes
stateVariables.invariant: Route.configured distinguishes unset from all-zero; path[0]==tokenIn and last-non-zero==tokenOut enforced at set time

structs.name: Route
fields: address[11] path (interleaved token/pool for Router NG)

externalEntryPoints.function: swap(address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint256 amountIn,uint256 minAmountOut) returns(uint256 amountOut)
externalEntryPoints.valueFlow: pulls amountIn tokenIn from caller -> approves router -> router swaps and sends output DIRECTLY to msg.sender (receiver). Returns router's reported amountOut. Reverts if route or reverse-route not configured, or amountIn==0.
externalEntryPoints.notes: permissionless is safe: caller funds its own swap and receives its own output; adapter is a stateless conduit
validates non-zero tokens, path[0]==tokenIn, last-non-zero==tokenOut; emits RouteSet

valueFlows.perSwap: tokenIn: caller -> adapter (amountIn) -> router (approval). tokenOut: router -> caller (receiver=msg.sender). Adapter retains nothing in the happy path.
valueFlows.residualRisk: if Curve exchange ever consumed < amountIn, leftover tokenIn dust and a stale router allowance could linger in the adapter (no rescue function); negligible for full-consume Curve exchange

externalCalls.trustLevel: trusted (registry: Curve Router NG is trusted)
externalCalls.notes: amountOut is taken from router's RETURN value, not a balance delta; minAmountOut is forwarded as the router's _expected slippage floor; receiver set to msg.sender so output never sits in the adapter

externalCalls.trustLevel: depends on caller; in protocol use it is underlyingToken or the vault share token

trustAssumptions: Curve Router NG at the hard-referenced address is trusted to honor minAmountOut and report true output (registry: Curve Router NG is trusted).
Owner correctly pre-computes and verifies route payloads off-chain (path/swapParams/pools, coin indices) -- setRoute only checks endpoints, not internal hop correctness.

Bidirectional routes are configured CONSISTENTLY: setRoute does not check that routes[B][A] is the true inverse of routes[A][B], only that the .configured flag is set (registry: bidirectional Curve route invariant assumed honored by deploy scripts / AMMRoutes.json).
Tokens are standard ERC20 (non-fee-on-transfer); FoT would make router output diverge from caller expectation.

localFindings.description: setRoute only validates path endpoints (path[0]==tokenIn, last-non-zero==tokenOut). swapParams [i,j,swap_type,pool_type,n_coins], the pools array, and reverse-route inverse-consistency are NOT validated on-chain. A misconfigured route (wrong coin index i/j, wrong pool) could swap into an unintended token or silently underperform; the bidirectional check verifies only the .configured FLAG of the reverse, not that it is the true inverse. Owner-trusted off-chain verification, but a non-obvious footgun for a one-direction-only mistake.
localFindings.recommendation: Treat AMMRoutes.json correctness and reverse-inverse consistency as a deploy-time review item; document that on-chain validation is endpoint-only.

localFindings.description: No sweep/rescue function. Any token accidentally sent to the adapter, or dust left if a router ever under-consumes amountIn, is permanently stranded (router output goes to msg.sender, not the adapter, so this is only an edge/operator concern).
localFindings.recommendation: Consider an onlyOwner rescue for stranded tokens, or accept as negligible given the stateless design.

scannerAttention: Permissionless swap() is benign in isolation (caller funds + receives its own swap), but confirm no integrator ever relies on the adapter holding balances.

Reverse-route inverse-consistency is an assumption, not an on-chain guarantee -- a half-correct bidirectional config passes isPairFullyConfigured but could misroute one direction. Cross-check against AMMRoutes.json USDe<->sUSDe entries (swapParams [0,1,1,10,2] forward vs [1,0,1,10,2] reverse).
router.exchange amountOut trusted as the realized amount (no balance-delta verification); fine under the trusted-router assumption, flag if that assumption is ever relaxed.
